scope: One order, one logical payment, bounded retry, cancellation and compensation
assumptions: The database transaction serializes payment and cancellation updates for one order.
A retry transition marked stutter may repeat, but weak fairness requires an enabled progress transition to eventually run.
Gateway callbacks are authenticated and contain an idempotency key.
Inventory is reserved after validation and released on cancellation, terminal failure or refund.

functional_contracts.responsibility: Validate trusted server data and persist the order atomically before payment is allowed.
functional_contracts.precondition: The request is new and no payment exists.
guarantees: Client-supplied prices never become the authoritative amount.
A persistence failure cannot leave an order payable with a partial inventory update.

functional_contracts.responsibility: Choose exactly one legal decision while the order is payable: start payment, cancel, or reject a duplicate/invalid request.
functional_contracts.precondition: Order is PAYMENT_PENDING, amount was verified and inventory is reserved.
guarantees: Payment and cancellation decisions are serialized.
A rejected or duplicate request cannot create another logical payment.

functional_contracts.responsibility: Resolve the gateway outcome with bounded retry and one idempotency key without interpreting timeout as decline.
functional_contracts.precondition: The order is payable and no successful payment has been committed.
guarantees: Only an authenticated definitive decline may end the payment flow as FAILED.
An UNKNOWN outcome keeps inventory reserved and is reconciled with the same idempotency key.
A successful charge is committed at most once.

functional_contracts.responsibility: Confirm a paid order or start compensation when confirmation cannot succeed.
guarantees: Confirmation retry never charges the customer again.
A paid order that cannot be confirmed enters compensation instead of FAILED.

functional_contracts.responsibility: Complete delivery or compensate a paid order that can no longer be fulfilled.
functional_contracts.precondition: Order is CONFIRMED and successful payment evidence is retained.
guarantees: Post-payment fulfillment failure always starts refund compensation.

functional_contracts.responsibility: Finish compensation idempotently and release inventory only with durable refund evidence.
functional_contracts.precondition: A successful charge exists and the order is REFUND_PENDING.
guarantees: Refund retry uses the same refund idempotency key.
A timeout cannot be treated as proof that no refund occurred.

functional_contracts.responsibility: Reject late mutation and return the stored result without reviving a terminal aggregate.
guarantees: No terminal state is revived by a late request or callback.
Repeated terminal operations are idempotent and auditable.

states.purpose: Receive an order request before trusting client data.

normal.action: Load server prices, validate quantities and reserve inventory.

incidents.problem: Invalid input, missing product or insufficient stock
incidents.detection: Validator and server-side product lookup reject the request
incidents.solution: Reject atomically; do not persist the order or reserve inventory

incidents.problem: Database error while reading products
incidents.detection: Database operation throws or transaction aborts
incidents.solution: Rollback and return a retryable error without creating an order

states.purpose: Represent an order whose server price, total and inventory have been checked.

normal.action: Persist order and items in the same transaction.

incidents.problem: Overflow or total mismatch discovered before commit
incidents.detection: Checked arithmetic or total equality assertion fails
incidents.solution: Rollback the transaction and release the reservation

incidents.problem: Persistence fails after inventory was reserved
incidents.detection: Save or commit fails
incidents.solution: Rollback all order and stock changes

states.purpose: Wait for a payment request while cancellation is still legal.

normal.action: Acquire the per-order transaction lock and record the idempotency key.

incidents.problem: Customer cancels before the gateway charge
incidents.detection: Cancellation wins the serialized state update
incidents.solution: Cancel the order and release reserved inventory

incidents.problem: Duplicate request with the same idempotency key
incidents.detection: Existing key is found for the order
incidents.solution: Return the existing in-progress result and create no second payment

incidents.problem: Payment amount differs from the server total
incidents.detection: Request amount is not equal to Order.TotalAmount
incidents.solution: Reject the payment; keep the order payable with the correct amount

states.purpose: Own the exclusive payment operation and wait for a gateway result.

normal.action: Persist one SUCCESS payment and transition the order atomically.

incidents.problem: Gateway timeout or transient network error
incidents.detection: No authenticated final response before timeout
incidents.solution: Release the lock and enter a bounded retry state using the same idempotency key

incidents.problem: Gateway permanently declines the charge
incidents.detection: Authenticated final decline response
incidents.solution: Mark the flow failed and release inventory

incidents.problem: Gateway charged but local database commit failed
incidents.detection: Payment remains PROCESSING while the gateway has a final result for the idempotency key
incidents.solution: Reconcile the existing charge by idempotency key; never create another logical payment

incidents.problem: Cancellation races with payment
incidents.detection: Cancellation observes payment lock or changed row version
incidents.solution: Serialize the operations; cancellation retries after the payment result

states.purpose: Resolve an unknown gateway outcome without creating a second logical charge.

normal.action: Use the final bounded attempt with the same idempotency key.

incidents.problem: Retry budget is exhausted while the gateway outcome remains unknown
incidents.detection: Bounded retry counter reaches its configured maximum without a final gateway result
incidents.solution: Stop automatic charging, keep inventory reserved and require reconciliation/manual review

incidents.problem: Customer cancels while no confirmed charge exists
incidents.detection: Gateway reconciliation confirms no successful charge
incidents.solution: Cancel and release inventory

states.purpose: Execute the final bounded payment reconciliation/attempt.

normal.action: Persist one SUCCESS payment and transition the order atomically.

incidents.problem: Final attempt is definitively declined
incidents.detection: Authenticated final decline proves no charge succeeded
incidents.solution: Mark failed and release inventory

incidents.problem: Final attempt times out with an unknown outcome
incidents.detection: No authenticated final response is available
incidents.solution: Stop charging automatically and continue reconciliation/manual review without releasing inventory

incidents.problem: Final attempt charged but local commit failed
incidents.detection: Payment remains PROCESSING while the gateway has a final result
incidents.solution: Reconcile the existing charge; do not increase the charge attempt counter

states.purpose: Represent exactly one successful payment whose amount matches the order.

normal.action: Confirm fulfillment and preserve the successful payment evidence.

incidents.problem: Duplicate success callback or client retry
incidents.detection: The order already has a SUCCESS payment for the idempotency key
incidents.solution: Return the original payment; do not insert or charge again

incidents.problem: Transient confirmation failure
incidents.detection: Fulfillment confirmation fails with a retryable error
incidents.solution: Keep PAID and retry confirmation without charging again

incidents.problem: Order cannot be fulfilled after payment
incidents.detection: Permanent inventory or fulfillment failure
incidents.solution: Start compensation; never silently change PAID to FAILED

states.purpose: Retry fulfillment confirmation without issuing another charge.

incidents.problem: Confirmation retry budget exhausted
incidents.detection: Bounded confirmation retry counter reaches its limit
incidents.solution: Escalate to compensating refund

states.purpose: Order is paid and accepted for fulfillment.

incidents.problem: Permanent fulfillment failure after confirmation
incidents.detection: The order cannot be delivered
incidents.solution: Start a refund and release inventory when compensation completes

states.purpose: Compensate a successful charge that cannot lead to completion.

normal.action: Persist refund evidence and release inventory.

incidents.problem: Refund gateway timeout
incidents.detection: No authenticated final refund result
incidents.solution: Retry or query with the same refund idempotency key and alert operations

incidents.problem: Late duplicate callback or state-change request
incidents.detection: Order is already terminal
incidents.solution: Return the stored result, reject state mutation and audit the event

states.purpose: Terminal state for a cancellation that won before a confirmed charge.

incidents.problem: Late payment request or callback
incidents.detection: Order is terminal CANCELLED
incidents.solution: Reject the charge/state mutation and raise an alert if the gateway reports money captured

states.purpose: Terminal observation for a request/order transaction rejected before any payment existed; the order row may not have been persisted.

incidents.problem: Late retry attempts to revive a rejected request
incidents.detection: The original create transaction was rejected or rolled back
incidents.solution: Reject mutation; require a corrected new request with a new operation identity

states.purpose: Terminal state when no successful charge exists and automatic recovery is exhausted.

incidents.problem: Late retry after terminal failure
incidents.detection: Order is terminal FAILED
incidents.solution: Reject mutation; require a new order rather than reviving this one

states.purpose: Terminal compensated state after a previously successful charge.

incidents.problem: Duplicate refund callback
incidents.detection: Refund transaction is already final
incidents.solution: Return the original refund result and do not refund twice

properties.label: violation
properties.description: No reachable state is explicitly unsafe.
Every paid state has successful payment evidence.
A cancelled order cannot contain a successful charge.
FAILED is used only when no successful charge exists.

properties.label: resource_conflict
properties.description: Payment and cancellation never own the critical resource simultaneously.
Every declared state is reachable from CREATED.
Every state documents detection, solution and next state for each incident.
Ignoring explicitly marked stutter retries, every reachable state inevitably reaches a terminal state.
Every state/event transition belongs to exactly one function and matches its declared outcome.
A terminal state can only reject/no-op and remain in the same terminal state.
A failure after successful payment can only preserve paid evidence or enter the refund path, never FAILED/CANCELLED.
An unknown payment outcome remains non-terminal with inventory reserved until an authoritative outcome is known.
Within one state, one event has exactly one declared next state.

negative_scenarios.description: A cancelled order is revived and paid.

incidents.problem: Illegal revival
incidents.detection: History monitor
incidents.solution: Reject transition

negative_scenarios.description: A mismatched amount is accepted as paid.

incidents.problem: Wrong amount accepted
incidents.detection: Amount invariant
incidents.solution: Reject payment

negative_scenarios.description: Two successful payments are persisted for one order.

incidents.problem: Duplicate charge
incidents.detection: Payment count
incidents.solution: Use idempotency and unique constraint

negative_scenarios.description: Payment and cancellation enter their critical sections together.

incidents.problem: Concurrent owners
incidents.detection: Lock ownership invariant
incidents.solution: Serialize with transaction/row lock

negative_scenarios.description: A paid order loses successful-payment evidence by moving directly to FAILED instead of compensation.
An unknown gateway outcome is incorrectly made terminal and inventory is released.

incidents.problem: Unknown result was closed
incidents.detection: Payment outcome remains UNKNOWN
incidents.solution: Keep reservation and reconcile

transition.action: BUG: release inventory before authoritative result
